action_items.text: Review the minutes from the last meeting posted on Project Share.
Investigate whether symbols on the remote control can be made more durable or fade-proof.
Investigate the feasibility of implementing a text-only TV guide preview feature instead of an LCD screen.
Research if there is a standard menu button usable across different TV brands to enable opening menus with a universal remote.
Develop a components concept for the new remote control.
Conduct trend-watching to understand what features people really want in a remote control.
Sketch ideas for the remote control design (e.g., shape, curves, colors) and present them at the next meeting.
Find out if rechargeable batteries are possible and if people are willing to pay extra for them.
Find out what people are willing to pay for the remote control (targeting around 25 Euros sales price).
Research the cost and space requirements for including an LCD screen on the remote.
Research the cost and space requirements for including speech recognition functionality on the remote.
Think of a name for the new remote control product.

decisions.text: The project will target younger people (under forty) who are willing to pay for a stylish and functional remote control.
The Teletext button should be kept but not made a primary button; it should be placed under a secondary menu option.
The corporate colors (black and yellow) and logo should be kept in mind for the design.
The team will pursue a universal remote control design rather than a brand-specific one.
Speech recognition will not be implemented in the remote control due to technical immaturity, memory constraints, and lack of market readiness.
The remote control should use durable materials (e.g., harder plastic) to prevent symbols from fading, potentially utilizing changeable covers.
The remote control design should be distinct from competitors (like Sony) to avoid confusion, possibly using different shapes or curves.
The power button should be placed on top of the remote.
The mute button should be placed near the volume selection, not at the top.
The channel buttons (up and down) should be placed on top of the remote.
The remote should include a beep and/or light feature to help deaf users or users who have lost the remote.
The remote should include an LCD screen to display information.
The channel buttons should be grouped together in a central section.
